evidence: The proposal workflow currently owns both lightweight scope and detailed design content.
The new requirements and design phases must feed the existing plan phase without losing plan graph auditability.
Implementation remains downstream of plan artifacts and should gain requirement/design traceability.
README workflow diagrams and artifact descriptions must reflect the phase split.
A lightweight proposal should be accepted before behavioral requirements are expanded.
Concrete behavioral requirements should drive design choices and make scope traceable.
Requirement nodes need edge records for citations, traceability, validation, and decay analysis.
Plan generation should consume requirements plus design rather than proposal-only design prose.
Plan phases should derive from the separate design artifact after requirements are validated.
OpenSpec's specs/delta spec model informs Cartographer-native requirements artifacts.
ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED requirements and scenarios map to graph-backed requirement nodes.
Existing JSONL validation and summary helpers can be extended to validate requirement graph artifacts.
Existing graph validation can add cross-artifact requirements/design/plan traceability checks.
New requirements graph must not duplicate existing authoritative plan state; it should add a separate behavioral contract layer.
The user clarified that accepted topic/change requirement deltas should fold into durable docs/requirements.md.
Topic-local requirements are deltas that become durable current behavior after implementation/archive.
Requirement IDs and scenario IDs should remain traceable when promoted into durable docs requirements.
Durable requirements should live under docs like ADRs live under docs/adr.
Human-readable design sections should have corresponding stable design graph nodes.
Design nodes need edges for requirement, fact, map, plan, validation, and receipt traceability.
Design decisions should explicitly satisfy or defer requirement IDs.
Plan generation should consume design IDs along with requirement IDs.
